Apple is where individual imaginations gather together, committing to the values that lead to great work. Every new product we build, service we create, or Apple Store experience we deliver is the result of us making each other’s ideas stronger. That happens because every one of us shares a belief that we can make something wonderful and share it with the world, changing lives for the better. It’s the diversity of our people and their thinking that inspires the innovation that runs through everything we do. When we bring everybody in, we can do the best work of our lives. Here, you’ll do more than join something — you’ll add something.
Apple Vision Pro is a revolutionary spatial computer that seamlessly blends digital content with your physical space. It will allow us to do the things we love in ways never before possible — all while staying connected to the people around us.
The Vision Products Group (VPG) is looking for a Senior Software Engineer to help us push the limits of the next generation of interactive experiences on our platform. This team is working with some of Apple’s most advanced technologies including spatial computing, augmented reality (AR), ARKit and Metal, to create groundbreaking new products. As a member of our organization, you will have the uniquely rewarding opportunity to craft future products that will delight and inspire millions of people every single day.
Apple makes the newest technologies accessible to create amazing and delightful user experiences. You will have the opportunity to work in a team to enhance the developer experience for spatial computing — improving user workflows and bringing new capabilities to the developers and creators building for our platform.
You will design and implement new features that fundamentally change how developers build new apps for our platforms. You care deeply about the customer experience and have a keen eye for detail where every interaction matters. You will drive solutions working in a dynamic environment in close collaboration with framework, tools, and product teams across Apple and VPG.
We're looking for an engineer with strong software engineering fundamentals and sharp product sensibility. You are comfortable across Xcode and the broader Apple developer toolchain, and you have shipped real software with Apple's frameworks and SDKs. You will help define the future of our developer tools and workflows — prototyping ideas, evaluating new technologies, building agentic and AI-assisted capabilities that plug into how engineers actually write, debug, test, and review code, working with designers and engineers to gather feedback, and ultimately shipping high-quality features to our customers. You understand the strengths and limitations of emerging technologies, including large language models, coding agents, and the protocols and tooling that connect them to a developer's environment, keep pace with the latest developments in the field, and have a strong instinct for where technology can meaningfully enhance a developer's workflow. Your passion for craft and user-focused product development will drive you to build amazing tools and features that enable and empower our customers to do their best work.
Design, build, and maintain developer tools, apps, CLIs, and SDKs that improve development workflows including agentic workflows
Partner with engineers and designers across Apple to drive definition and implementation of key features needed to enhance the developer experience for spatial computing
Set technical direction for the developer experience and own tools end to end: requirements, architecture, implementation, documentation, release, and long-term maintenance
Build and operate the measurement, profiling, and analysis of developer features and tooling, driving towards power and performance targets in close collaboration with feature and performance teams throughout the software development release
Mentor engineers and provide technical leadership across the team by raising engineering standards through code review and guidelines
Minimum Qualifications
7+ years of software engineering experience
BS/MS in Computer Science OR equivalent degree OR equivalent experience
Proven industry experience working with developer tools: developing, debugging, and profiling apps
Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to drive alignment across multiple partner teams
Proven track record of shipping user-facing products or features, with a passion for end-user impact
Preferred Qualifications
Strong proficiency in Swift, Objective-C, C/C++
Hands-on experience with Apple developer tools and frameworks
Detail-oriented approach to solving problems and building new features
Prior work as a technical lead for coordinating cross-functional collaboration
Self-motivated approach to improving customer workflows with an eye toward product quality and user experience
Experience developing software using generative AI
Experience developing agent skills and AI evaluation plans

Our team is looking for a talented Software Engineer to help evolve the application developer experience that Apple's engineering teams rely on to ship safely and quickly. You'll join a team responsible for the systems that govern how changes move to production: change tracking, approvals and risk assessment, release coordination, and audit and compliance workflows. You'll help modernize these services, integrate them with build, deployment, and hotfix pipelines, and scale them to meet growing demand, with opportunities to enhance them using AI-driven tools and practices. This role blends proven engineering practices with forward-looking approaches in agentic AI, intelligent automation, and process simplification. You'll collaborate closely with project managers, partner platform teams, and SREs to translate clear requirements into production services that are performant, resilient, and continually improving.
Imagine empowering hundreds of developers across Apple Service Engineering to plan, approve, and release changes to their services faster, more safely, and with far less toil.
At Apple, we don't just build products, we craft experiences that redefine entire ecosystems. The Application Developer Experience team owns the services that govern how changes reach production across Apple's platform engineering teams every day: change tracking, approvals and risk assessment, release coordination, and audit and compliance workflows. Join us to develop the next generation of Apple's cloud services infrastructure.
As a Software Engineer on the Developer Experience team, you'll play a key role in modernizing large-scale change management systems. You'll untangle years of legacy process and tooling, standardize on a single, well-integrated path from change request to production, and build agentic AI systems that assess change risk, triage failed or blocked changes, and support developers autonomously. This is about designing robust, scalable systems that let hundreds of developers propose, validate, and release changes efficiently, while continuously simplifying the platform underneath them.
We're seeking engineers with a strong foundation in backend development who are also excited about applying AI, including agentic, tool-using systems, in practical, impactful ways. If you're energized by challenges that span distributed systems, change and release tooling, integrations with build and deployment pipelines, and autonomous intelligent agents, and you're ready to work on systems used by engineering teams across Apple, we'd love to hear from you.
Join us, and help craft the future of change management at Apple.
Design and build backend services for change management. Own the services behind change tracking, approvals, risk assessment, and release coordination. They need to be performant, resilient, and scalable for hundreds of developers.
Modernize legacy systems. Untangle legacy change-management tooling and processes, and migrate them to a single, well-integrated path from change request to production.
Integrate with build, deployment, and hotfix pipelines. Connect change management services to partner platform systems so changes, approvals, and releases flow reliably end to end. This includes emergency and hotfix changes.
Build intelligent automation. Design tool-using AI agents that assess change risk, triage failed or blocked changes, and support developers autonomously. Apply AI-driven practices to improve the services themselves.
Translate requirements into production systems. Work with project managers, partner platform teams, and SREs to turn clear requirements into shipped, well-tested services.
Operate and improve what you ship. Take part in monitoring, incident response, and on-call as needed. Use that experience to improve reliability and reduce developer toil.
Simplify the platform. Keep reducing complexity, duplication, and manual steps, so developers need less effort to ship.
Minimum Qualifications
2+ years of industry experience building backend systems.
Strong programming skills in Java and Python.
Familiarity with utilizing and developing AI-driven and agentic tools to improve workflows and productivity.
Knowledge of algorithms, data structures, and distributed systems principles.
Experience with databases (relational and/or NoSQL) and scalable service architectures.
Excellent communication skills and a collaborative mindset.
BS, MS or PhD in Computer Science/Engineering
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with containerization and standardized image-based deployment workflows.
Familiarity with AI/ML frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow) and LLM libraries (e.g., LangChain, Hugging Face), or building AI-assisted developer and on-call tooling.
Experience building agentic AI systems - LLM agents, tool/function calling, orchestration frameworks, or agent SDKs (e.g., Claude, MCP, LangGraph).
Experience with large-scale codebase migrations and multi-repo tooling.
Experience with messaging systems (e.g., Kafka) and microservices architectures.
Passion for developer experience and empathy for building tools that empower other engineers.

As a Cellular Modem RF Software Engineering Program Manager, you will be at the heart of our ground-breaking cellular baseband modems to meet performance, quality and schedule requirements for Apple products. This role demands excellent interpersonal skills to work multi-functionally within a dynamic engineering environment. Partnering with engineers and managers from our hardware and software engineering teams, will be key to your success in this role. You will deliver executive communication and presentations to support the decision-making process, clearly and effectively communicate overall program status, while identifying and resolving key bottlenecks and interdependencies of sophisticated projects. Ideally, you will also have validated project management experience in some aspect of RF Software development, integration and pre / post-silicon RF verification, and cellular RF features.
Own the development of Cellular RF Software controlling the RF transceivers and Front-end components in real-time full signaling mode.
Track execution for RF Software plans across project phases from implementation and pre-silicon validation to cellular feature bring-up.
Manage productization of RF Software through cellular modem system testing, field testing, interoperability testing, and production ramp.
Drive and report RF Software activities for development, validation, non-regression testing, release management, improvements and defect resolution.
Anticipate risks, develop mitigation strategies and facilitate conflict resolution.
Deliver presentations supporting executive reviews including project status, key metrics, top risks and issues.
Minimum Qualifications
BS and 10+ years relevant industry experience.
Demonstrated ability with a track record of hands-on engineering management / leadership or program / project management in the FW/SW domain.
Relevant proven experience in wireless modem Layer 1 / RF Software development and/or RF verification.
Preferred Qualifications
Good understanding about the Development Lifecycle for embedded software / firmware.
Good understanding about Development Lifecycle for embedded software.
Knowledge of cellular modem baseband building blocks and software layers.
Good understanding of RF transceiver and RF front end components control for cellular modems.
Knowledge of RF Cellular major features, real-time requirements and associated challenges.
Experience in wireless standards a significant plus (5G-NR/4G LTE/UMTS/GSM/CDMA).
Ability to quickly establish and manage sophisticated multi-functional relationships in a dynamic engineering environment.
Creative problem solver with ability to lead technical teams and multi-functional groups against plans.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills at senior management level including strong presentation skills.

We are a small, close-knit team of engineers building the experiences that let people view, place, and share 3D content across Apple platforms, including Apple Vision Pro. We believe 3D should feel as effortless as opening a photo, and we sweat the details that make that true. Join us to shape how millions of people explore and interact with the world around them in a new design space, and to build the frameworks that other teams across Apple build on.
This role focuses on designing and building the user-facing 3D and spatial experiences, and the front-end architecture beneath them, that bring digital content into people's physical world. You will combine strong UI engineering with real-time 3D, working closely with design and partner teams to ship polished, performant, and scalable features. You will also help define how shared, multi-user spatial experiences come to life.
Design and build interactive 3D and spatial user interfaces that feel natural, responsive, and delightful across Apple platforms.
Develop scalable, maintainable front-end components that multiple platforms and product surfaces can share.
Contribute to multi-user experiences that let people view and interact with the same 3D content together.
Collaborate with design, product, and partner engineering teams to turn novel AR/VR interaction concepts into shipping features.
Profile and optimize real-time rendering and UI performance to maintain smooth frame rates and low latency.
Help build and evolve the APIs that enable spatial experiences.
Participate actively in code reviews and design discussions, and share what you learn with the team.
Minimum Qualifications
2+ years of professional software engineering experience building and shipping production applications or frameworks.
Proficiency in Swift, Objective-C, or C++, with experience building user interfaces on Apple platforms.
Hands-on experience with real-time 3D graphics or 3D UI, such as games, game engines, or 3D frameworks. Professional, academic, or personal projects all count.
Demonstrated ability to own features from design through shipping.
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Experience using AI coding tools as part of your regular workflow, with the ability to critically review, verify, and debug AI-generated code.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with scalable front-end architecture, including modular, reusable components shared across products.
Experience building multi-user or multiplayer experiences, including state synchronization and shared sessions.
Familiarity with Apple frameworks, platforms, and design principles (e.g. SwiftUI, UIKit, RealityKit, ARKit, SharePlay).
Passion for UI/UX and for exploring the design space of AR/VR and spatial computing.
Curiosity about how generative AI is changing software development, and eagerness to explore, adopt, and share new AI-assisted workflow practices with the team.
Experience partnering effectively with design, product, and other cross-functional teams to ship high-quality work.
Comfortable navigating ambiguity and adapting quickly as priorities evolve.
Interest in API design for frameworks used by developers.

AI systems are only as trustworthy as the methods used to evaluate them. At Apple, where AI powers experiences for billions of people, getting evaluation right is not a support function, it is a foundational science. Our team, part of Apple Services Engineering, is building that scientific foundation: rigorous, scalable evaluation methodology for LLMs, agentic systems, and human-AI interaction. Our goal is evidence that teams can act on: what to measure, whether a change helped, why a system failed, and whether it is ready to ship.
What makes this team unusual is its interdisciplinary core. You will work alongside measurement scientists (psychometrics, validity theory), ML researchers, and platform engineers, bringing together ML research, statistical rigor, and production engineering.
We are looking for an Applied Scientist who works across the full arc of evaluation science: turning research into tools engineers can use on their own, and turning what those engineers run into new research. You care whether a method holds up on real data, at real scale, for a real decision, and you are curious enough to go after the open question underneath when it doesn't.
Our team is building self-service evaluation: tools, SDKs, and AI-powered capabilities that let engineers across Apple evaluate their AI features on their own, quickly and correctly, so they can build and ship those features faster. You will develop the methods that make this possible: raising the quality of the evaluations engineers run, and helping them understand what their results mean and what to do next. Often the method a problem needs doesn't exist yet. When that happens, you will figure it out, whether that means extending a recent paper or developing something new, and share what you learn through publications and internal research reports. We are looking for individuals across a range of experience levels.
With research and measurement scientists, you will co-develop new methods, make sure the tools give engineers valid, trustworthy signals, and bring back the hard problems that should shape the team's research agenda. With platform and research engineers, you will define what each method needs to work reliably without an expert in the loop, including its assumptions, failure modes, and validation tests, so it can ship in the evaluation SDKs and APIs used across Apple.
The successful candidate combines scientific depth with practical judgment: you know which methods fit a problem and why, can design experiments that show whether they actually work, can diagnose why they break down on messy real-world data, and can explain clearly what an evaluation result does and does not support.
Develop and adapt methods that raise the quality of the evaluations engineers run on LLMs and agentic systems.
Build and improve the ML capabilities behind the team's developer-facing evaluation tools, such as rubric and test-set generation, automated judging, and failure analysis. Work with measurement scientists to integrate validity frameworks and psychometric methods, so the tools measure what they claim to measure and give developers the right signals.
Develop ways for engineers to understand what their evaluation results mean and what to do next, such as uncertainty, likely failure causes, and when a result shouldn't be trusted. Partner with measurement scientists on how results are reported.
Learn where engineers get stuck when evaluating AI features, and turn their recurring questions ("is this better?", "why did this fail?", "is it ready to ship?") into capabilities the tools can answer.
Design and run large-scale experiments that test whether methods hold up on production data, including robustness to distribution shift across domains and languages, applying the team's statistical and validity standards for reliability and uncertainty.
Prototype methods in well-structured Python, and partner with research and platform engineers to productionize them into evaluation SDKs, APIs, and services, owning the scientific correctness of what ships.
When existing methods fall short, develop new ones with research and measurement scientists. Turn recurring gaps into open problems for the team's research agenda, and share findings through publications at top-tier venues and internal research reports.
Communicate findings, limitations, and recommendations clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.
Minimum Qualifications
Ph.D. in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Statistics, or a closely related field, or a Master's degree in one of these fields with 3+ years of applied research experience.
Deep expertise in evaluating AI systems, gained through research on evaluation methods, substantial hands-on experience evaluating LLMs or agentic systems in real products, or both.

Join us in shaping the future of Generative AI at Apple! Are you passionate about making AI systems safer, more inclusive, and globally representative? Apple is seeking a Machine Learning Platform Engineer to build the tooling and infrastructure behind our Responsible AI mitigations, from on-device foundation models running on Apple Silicon to server-side inference on Private Cloud Compute (PCC). In this role, you will build the Python platform our ML and safety engineers rely on to train, evaluate, deploy, and configure safety classifiers, guardrail models, and model behavior overrides. You will turn manual, one-off workflows into automated, scalable, and reproducible systems, so that every evaluation runs the same way, every deployment is validated, and every configuration change is safe to ship
Our team leads Responsible AI initiatives for global generative AI products, operating at the intersection of policy, product, and GenAI. We build the safety guardrails, and policy enforcement layers that protect users from unintended model behavior. This role builds the platform underneath that work. You will build the systems that enable consistent training and evaluation at scale: an training/evaluation platform that runs any benchmark the same way every time, deployment pipelines that package and release models and mitigation assets to devices and the cloud, and tooling that lets engineers across many languages and modalities author and validate configuration changes with confidence. You will also dig into the failures and regressions the platform surfaces, and turn them into concrete fixes. ML engineers, client engineers, policy, and release teams are your customers, and you will need enough understanding of how models are evaluated and served to build infrastructure whose results they can trust.
Evaluation Platform: Design and build a scalable, automated platform for running evaluations of safety classifiers, guardrail models, and overrides consistently, including job orchestration, reproducible run configurations, versioned datasets and results, and regression reporting between model and configuration versions
Model Deployment Infrastructure: Own the infrastructure responsible for packaging, versioning, validating, and shipping production ML models and mitigation assets across release trains, from build through rollout and rollback
Configuration & Overrides Tooling: Build the schemas, validation, and automated tests for the configuration files that control model behavior (overrides, deny lists, thresholds, per-feature policy), so every change is checked for correctness, scope, and unintended impact before it reaches users
Inference Tooling: Build Python libraries, services, and CLIs that let teams run guardrail and foundation models the same way production does, including preprocessing and normalization parity, so evaluation results represent what ships
Error Analysis & Data Pipelines: Build the pipelines that manage evaluation datasets and results, run error analyses on the failures and regressions they surface, and turn findings into concrete model, data, or configuration fixes, while ensuring data handling meets Apple privacy and retention policies
Platform Adoption & Automation: Make the platform self-serve for adopting teams, automating repetitive authoring and review steps (including with LLM-assisted and agentic tooling) so engineers spend their time on judgment, not mechanics
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with ML, client, and release engineering teams to understand their workflows and translate them into reliable, performant infrastructure, and represent the platform in architecture and design reviews
Minimum Qualifications
3+ years of professional engineering experience, with Python as a primary development language
BS in Computer Science, Mathematics, Statistics, or a related field, or equivalent industry experience
Experience building infrastructure or tooling for ML inference, evaluation, or deployment that is used by engineers outside your direct team
Experience building or operating infrastructure that deploys ML models to production and maintains them across versions
Working knowledge of how ML models are evaluated (metrics, held-out test sets, error analysis, sources of non-reproducibility), enough to build evaluation infrastructure whose results ML engineers can trust
Experience designing configuration-driven systems, including schemas, validation, versioning, and safe rollout of config changes
Strong software engineering fundamentals: testing, CI/CD, code review, and writing maintainable code that others build on
Excellent communication skills and the ability to explain technical tradeoffs to cross-functional partners
Must be comfortable working with sensitive or potentially offensive content
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with LLM inference, including tokenization, batching, streaming, and serving frameworks
Working knowledge of on-device ML runtimes (Core ML, MLX, or equivalent) and the model-export lifecycle: converting trained models into shippable assets and loading them at runtime
Experience running distributed evaluation or workflow orchestration at scale (Kubernetes, Ray, Spark, or equivalent)
Experience with text normalization, pattern-based filtering, or multilingual NLP
Experience with Responsible AI, trust and safety, or content moderation systems
Experience building LLM-based or agentic developer tooling
Familiarity with Swift

Strong software engineering fundamentals: testing, CI/CD, code review, and writing maintainable code that others build on
Excellent communication skills and the ability to explain technical tradeoffs to cross-functional partners

Working knowledge of on-device ML runtimes (Core ML, MLX, or equivalent) and the model-export lifecycle: converting trained models into shippable assets and loading them at runtime
Experience running distributed evaluation or workflow orchestration at scale (Kubernetes, Ray, Spark, or equivalent)

Do you want to help build some of the largest and most consequential enterprise and customer technology systems in the world? Join Apple’s Information Systems and Technology (IS&T) organization.
IS&T is the engine behind everything Apple does for customers and for the people who build for them. It’s Apple’s central nervous system. Supporting 2.5 billion active Apple devices, processing billions of secure transactions, and keeping the technology that defines modern life running flawlessly, IS&T makes the impossible feel effortless.
Customer Systems is part of IS&T and drives the technology behind Apple's customer support experience — from contact center operations to the software powering the iconic Genius Bar. The team also builds and operates AppleCare's online support platform, which handles 6 billion visits per year, delivering seamless, high-quality support to Apple customers around the globe.
Design and build microservices powering low-latency, high-throughput customer experiences — serving over a million users daily across Apple Support websites, iOS apps, and phone-based frontends.
Own end-to-end delivery of features — from technical design and implementation through testing, deployment, and production observability.
Drive engineering best practices — code reviews, unit/integration testing, CI/CD pipeline improvements, and documentation — raising the bar for the broader team.
Architect non-blocking, event-driven service pipelines that handle millions of concurrent requests with resilience and back-pressure management.
Contribute to API design and contract-first development, ensuring backward compatibility and clean integration across service boundaries.
Minimum Qualifications
B.S. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent professional work experience.
5+ years proven experience developing software in a professional capacity. Longer experience preferred.
2+ years proven experience with Java, including proficiency in concurrency, memory management, and performance optimization techniques.
Proficiency in OOP principles, data structures, algorithms, and software design patterns (e.g. GoF), with a proven focus on implementing testable, maintainable, and extensible backend code.
Experience building production applications with the Spring ecosystem (e.g. Spring Boot, Spring MVC, Spring Security, Spring Data, Spring Cloud, etc.), including proficiency in dependency injection, auto-configuration, reactive programming with WebFlux, and designing microservices using Spring-based patterns.
Solid understanding of advanced JVM internals (e.g. garbage collection, memory allocation, JIT, JNI, etc.).
Experience designing, implementing, and shipping high-scale, high-performance, highly available, fault-tolerant, and secure cloud-based distributed systems.
Solid knowledge of networking concepts, protocols, and infrastructure (e.g. HTTP/HTTPS, TCP/IP, CDN, load balancing, edge computing, DNS, Zero Trust architecture, etc.).
Preferred Qualifications
Track record of leading software projects within a team as a tech lead (TL), while mentoring software engineers.
Hands-on experience leveraging GenAI coding tools (e.g., Claude, Copilot, Codex) to accelerate the software development lifecycle, enhance code quality, and streamline debugging and testing processes.
Experience with complementary programming languages beyond Java (e.g. Go, Python, Ruby, etc.), including practical use for automation scripting, infrastructure tooling, data processing pipelines, and build system customizations.
Experience in API design and implementation, including proficiency in RESTful API principles, gRPC, GraphQL, contract-first design (e.g. OpenAPI/Swagger, Protobuf, etc.), API versioning strategies, gateway patterns, rate limiting, and designing APIs for backward compatibility and long-term evolution.
Experience with caching strategies and in-memory data technologies (e.g. Redis, Memcached, Hazelcast, Ehcache, etc.), including proficiency in cache invalidation patterns, distributed caching architectures, and session management for high-throughput applications.
